answers.M8-S1: The author tests whether his Mason-bees can find their way home from far away, and despite injuries and wind, some return quickly, showing a strong homing ability.
answers.M8-S2: To show that conditions made the trip even harder: the bees had to fly low and couldn't see the land, which makes their successful return more impressive.
answers.M8-S3: The bees weren't struggling or lost; they found their way easily enough to stop and gather food on the way, yet still got home fast.
answers.M8-S4: So he could tell his released bees apart from other bees, letting Aglaé recognize which ones returning to the nest were his test bees.
answers.M8-S5: He goes from doubting any bees would make it home to being surprised and impressed when he learns two returned quickly.
answers.M8-S6: In time order, as a narrative of the experiment: setting it up, releasing the bees, the problems, then the result.
answers.M8-S7: To show how fast and impressive the bees' return was: over two and a half miles in under forty-five minutes, even while stopping to forage.
answers.M8-S8: To explain a difficulty that weakened the experiment and to be honest that only about half the bees were in good shape to try returning.
answers.M8-S9: That they couldn't find their way by seeing landmarks from above, so they must have found home some other way, which makes their return remarkable.
